title: Non-REM sleep has three stages, and the deepest one comes mostly early
summary: NHLBI says non-REM sleep has three stages, and that stage 3, deep or slow-wave sleep, usually takes more of the early night.
body: NHLBI defines the three non-REM stages from brain-activity measurements in sleep studies. Stage 1 is the transition between wakefulness and sleep. Stage 2 is when the person is asleep. Stage 3 is called deep sleep or slow-wave sleep, after a pattern in those measurements, and a person usually spends more time in it early in the night. An OpenStax psychology chapter divides non-REM differently. That difference is its own card. This card is only the three-stage account NHLBI prints.

sources.title: How Sleep Works: Sleep Phases and Stages
